what: L-8 event-loop occupancy attribution for the three named blocking sources
protocol: section 4.4: min-of-N batches, median-of-M, warm-up, gc.collect(), absolute ceiling
limits_relaxed_note: Phase 1 (the three per-call costs) ran with NO app and therefore at production limits; it is the phase-1 numbers alone that carry a production-limit claim. Phase 2 ran with the eight rate limits relaxed, because at production limits the probe's own requests are answered 429 by the limiter and 403 by auto-ban before reaching any of the three sites.
phase1_was_uninstrumented_note: Phase 1 ran BEFORE install_instruments(). Each phase-1 measurement also refuses to report a figure if its own source charged the meter during the run, so this cannot silently regress into a figure that includes the instrument.
stdout_redirect_note: Both phases run with fd 1 pointed at /dev/null. structlog still runs every record through ConsoleRenderer, so the exc_info formatting this harness is measuring stays inside the measurement; what is excluded is the terminal write, which is not the application's work. Unredirected, the ~10 000 phase-1 renders alone cost ~620 s of CPU and buried the number they were measuring. stderr is never redirected.

guarded.note: The two arms yield the same object on the installed API version; what differs is whether the tracer's span machinery was entered. The delta prices THAT difference, not a span allocation.

proxy_tracer.note: The two arms yield the same object on the installed API version; what differs is whether the tracer's span machinery was entered. The delta prices THAT difference, not a span allocation.

span_guard_ab.delta_verdict: RESOLVABLE: the dead arm's fastest batch minimum (3.0170 us) exceeds the guarded arm's slowest (0.9260 us), so the arms do not overlap.
span_guard_ab.separation_rule: the two arms are separated only when the dead arm's FASTEST batch minimum exceeds the guarded arm's SLOWEST one, i.e. when their batch minima do not overlap at all; the delta is reported but is not a result unless they are

cross_check.verdict: REFUTED: the three sources are a negligible share of observed loop lag
cross_check.note: accounted is the load-bearing number: it is CPU time charged to the process inside the three sites, divided by CPU time the thread actually consumed. injected extrapolates the microbenchmark per-call cost and therefore also counts time the sites did not block the loop (sockets, syscalls). A large gap between them is itself a finding: it means the three sites are called often but rarely block. The denominator is the grid occupancy, not sum(lag): see occupancy_naive_lag_sum_note.

loop_lag.occupancy_naive_lag_sum_note: sum(lag) over an absolute-grid sampler double-counts any block longer than one interval, so it exceeds 1.0 and even exceeds the wall clock under starvation. Recorded unclamped as evidence of that degeneracy, never used as a denominator.
loop_lag.sampler_cost_note: the sampler's own cost is inside total_s and is bounded per sample by SAMPLER_COST_CEILING_US (100 us)
